tn-shelby-2026-collierville-alderman-2-j.name: Jewel Jordan
tn-shelby-2026-collierville-alderman-2-j.bio: Collierville resident of over 50 years who serves on the town Planning Commission and Police Advisory Board.

tn-shelby-2026-collierville-alderman-2-k.name: Chad Kelsey
tn-shelby-2026-collierville-alderman-2-k.bio: Lifelong Collierville resident and community volunteer who has served on the town's Historic District Commission and with Main Street Collierville.

positions.stance: Works to preserve "the character, safety, and quality of life" that make Collierville home, respecting its history and neighborhoods.
Promotes responsible economic growth to support local businesses and strengthen the town's long-term future without losing what makes it unique.
Believes taxpayers should be protected through "transparent leadership, careful budgeting, and accountable decision-making," with public safety and infrastructure as priorities.
Central to his mission is activating vacant commercial spaces in Collierville with businesses that meet residents' needs.

tn-shelby-2026-collierville-alderman-4-d.name: Liz Deely
tn-shelby-2026-collierville-alderman-4-d.bio: Former business professional with General Motors, DuPont, Merrill Lynch and CPS Color, and a former substitute teacher and adjunct business instructor.

positions.stance: Believes residents deserve town leadership that is "open, accessible, and accountable to the people it serves."
Will work to keep government spending responsible, protect taxpayer dollars, and ensure the budget reflects residents' priorities.
Will stand with Collierville's police, firefighters, and first responders to keep families and neighborhoods safe.
Will protect the character and quality of life that have made Collierville a great place to live for generations.
Will respect homeowners' rights, "support responsible growth, and stop overdevelopment."

tn-shelby-2026-collierville-alderman-4-m.name: Missy Marshall
tn-shelby-2026-collierville-alderman-4-m.bio: Collierville alderman since 2020 and Executive Director of Keep Tennessee Beautiful.

tn-shelby-2026-germantown-mayor-babian-e.name: Edgar Babian
tn-shelby-2026-germantown-mayor-babian-e.bio: Retired Germantown Fire Department deputy chief with 40 years in the department and former Fire Chief of Rossville.

positions.stance: Honor the city's agreements with residents, maintain Germantown to the standard families deserve, and "restore the hometown feeling."
Lower taxes, reduce spending, freeze property taxes for seniors, and cut garbage fees.
Supports term limits of "two terms, then at least one term off" for elected officials.
Modernize crime prevention and fully fund police and fire to keep Germantown one of Tennessee's safest cities.
Fight to bring Germantown Elementary and Middle School back in 2032 and protect Germantown High School.

tn-shelby-2026-germantown-mayor-salvaggi.name: Tony Salvaggio
tn-shelby-2026-germantown-mayor-salvaggi.bio: Germantown alderman, owner of Memphis Door & Hardware, and licensed residential and commercial general contractor who owns The Salvaggio Group.

positions.stance: "Evaluating and strengthening our police, fire, and emergency services" as the foundation of safe neighborhoods.
Protecting and responsibly funding Germantown Municipal School District to ensure excellence for generations.
Supports "a comprehensive assessment of City spending" so every dollar is managed wisely and transparently.
Supports thoughtful, well-planned, aesthetically appropriate development that protects Germantown's character and preserves its limited land.
Restoring citizens' trust "through open communication, fiscal clarity, and principled leadership."

tn-shelby-2026-germantown-alderman-2-gib.name: Mary Anne Gibson
tn-shelby-2026-germantown-alderman-2-gib.bio: Germantown alderman and vice mayor, former Shelby County Board of Education commissioner, and residential real estate affiliate broker with The Firm.

tn-shelby-2026-lakeland-mayor-mccarter-c.name: Connie McCarter
tn-shelby-2026-lakeland-mayor-mccarter-c.bio: Lakeland Commissioner since 2022 and a registered nurse and healthcare educator for 47 years.

positions.stance: Supports Neighborhood Watch programs using already-appropriated funds and collaboration with the Shelby County Sheriff's Office for fast response times.
"Strong, consistent support for the Lakeland School System" and lasting educational excellence for every student.
Invest in road maintenance so every neighborhood has safe, well-maintained streets, fixing problems before they become expensive repairs.
Enhance Lakeland's parks and recreational spaces so families have places to gather and enjoy the outdoors.
Encourage responsible, sustainable growth that strengthens the tax base without raising tax rates on current residents.
